hero.headline: Understand the product
hero.subline: FlintFlow helps you clarify the idea, write the requirements and check them back the way an experienced BA does. The result is an SRS your dev team and your AI coding tools can both rely on.

facts.phases: 12 phases, every step approved by you

check.title: Three-tier check
check.flags: red flags · {amber} amber flags to review

how.title: A BA's process, split into 12 phases.
how.subline: AI drafts one part at a time. You accept it or ask for changes before anything moves on.

clarify.title: Clarify
clarify.body: Tell us the idea or upload what you already have. FlintFlow only asks about what is still missing.

analyze.title: Analyze
analyze.body: Facts separated from assumptions, contradictions and gaps pointed out. The Brief must be approved before any SRS is written.

specify.title: Specify
specify.body: Use cases, non-functional requirements, use case diagrams and the ERD are drafted one part at a time.

verify.title: Verify
verify.body: Checked against the template, against ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 and on the quality of each requirement. Red flags block the baseline.

modes.title: Start from whatever you already have.

fpt.title: New, on the FPT template
fpt.body: You only have an idea and a few notes. FlintFlow takes you from the Brief to a full SRS on the FPT template.

client.title: On the client's template
client.body: Upload the template your client requires. FlintFlow reads its structure, drafts only the sections it asks for and fills them straight into that file.

existing.title: Revise an existing SRS
existing.body: Import the .docx you already use to see what it is missing. When the client changes a requirement, the edits show up as Track Changes inside the file.

workspace.headline: AI proposes.
workspace.subline: Nothing reaches the document without you: accept it, ask for changes, or take the question back to the client.

chat.user: Citizens file building permit applications online, an officer reviews them and returns the decision…
chat.title: 2 questions before writing use cases
chat.q1: Who reviews the application: the district office or the department?
chat.q2: Do buildings above 7 floors need extra paperwork?
chat.note: Question 2 decides whether the review flow has to branch.
